line: item.set(delta) is the one API, and the delta is the saved line
detail: You change an Item with one call. The same object, wrapped in the path down to the item, is what gets saved.

line: Nested names down to the target; the key's spelling says what it does (D13)
detail: A line walks down by name. A plain key is data (or a step into a child), `name()` calls a method, and `#id` picks a list item. An index would point at a different item after someone inserts above it.

line: List, Page and Ref stay Items; Ref forwards with moved_to
detail: No renames. A Ref points at an item somewhere else, and a moved item leaves a forward that Ref follows.

line: One writer per file, and one home per page
detail: Only one process appends to a file, so no two writers fight over it. A page lives in one place; other places hold a Ref, not a second copy.

line: Every line gets seq, client and n; the sender gets an ack
detail: The server numbers each line (seq). The writer adds client and n, so a retry is saved once. The sender hears an ack instead of its own echo.

line: Changes save through this.store.change(); events are for views only
detail: Your F6. A change calls the nearest store directly, so a tab page with no bubbling still saves. The change event stays for views.

line: add writes the whole item; adding an owned item makes a Ref
detail: The add line carries the full envelope (id, type, data, child lists), so a replay gives back exactly what you built. Your F7: an item that already has a parent is added as a Ref.

line: Views bind through item.prop(key), not hand-wired events
detail: item.prop(key) is the Property.of you already built. A view takes the handle, keeps the unbind, and writes back through item.set.

line: Room plus Journal: JSONL now, SQLite next, Durable Object later
detail: The Room is plain JS that knows lines and seq, never Items. The Journal passed into it decides where the lines live.

line: Presence as a throwaway frame: soft locks, cursors, typing dots
detail: Presence is relayed to the other tabs and never written to the log. A soft lock is just presence that expires 30 s after it stops.

line: No CRDTs, fractional positions or offline multi-writer before phase 5
detail: Order stays a plain list of ids with an after. Merging by several offline writers is a later phase, and it needs its own tests first.

line: Never log anything faster than a few changes a second
detail: Game ticks, audio/video and every keystroke are streams, not lines. Send them live, and save the result as one Item change.
